patch.summary:
Thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Five9 share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.

Comparison thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs. Choose Dialpad only if your buying job matches “AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard fr” rather than Five9's shape. Choose Five9 only if your buying job matches “Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/E” rather than Dialpad's shape. Workflow advantage: Dialpad leans business-phone, team-communication; Five9 leans contact-center, customer-messaging. Trade-off: you gain focus on one product's motion at the cost of the other's adjacent coverage — no universal winner.

Major differences:
- Buyer thesis: Overlapping use cases, different tradeoffs — Dialpad and Five9 share buyer workflows; choose based on documented strengths and limits.
- Positioning: Dialpad is AI-first cloud phone (Dialpad Connect) with included transcription/summaries — Standard from $15/user/month annual; Sell and Support are sep; Five9 is Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; Plus/Pro/Enterprise quote — 50-seat minimum..
- Company-size focus: Dialpad (small-business, mid-market, enterprise) vs Five9 (mid-market, enterprise).
- Workflow coverage skew: Dialpad-leaning business-phone, team-communication vs Five9-leaning contact-center, customer-messaging.
- Researched limits: Dialpad — Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Five9 — 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers.

Limitations — Dialpad: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price; Connect Pro has a 3-user minimum; Enterprise requires 100 users; Five9: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers; Digital is non-voice; Core is the published voice+digital entry.

Poor-fit cases: Dialpad is a poor fit when that limitation bites: Pricing page is product-tab heavy — Connect vs Support vs Sell can confuse buyers comparing a single seat price · Five9 is a poor fit when that limitation bites: 50 concurrent-seat minimum — not viable for small SMB phone buyers · Avoid Dialpad if you actually need Five9's motion (Cloud contact center (CCaaS) — Digital from $119/concurrent seat/mo; Core $159; )

Neither product has a completed hands-on product test on SoftwareGlimpse — this comparison is research/data-based only.
